idea.value: A typed query pulls one complete person out of a faceless crowd, shows every field it knows about them, and then shows that every face in the crowd is just as complete.

audience.value: Technical buyers who need contact data in their own tools: developers and growth or sales teams at small software companies. The query names founders of small developer-tool companies, the record lists email, social handles and city, and the sign-off names a people-search product.

value.device: A white frame becomes a crowd in five frames, and a search field types a precise, slightly ironic query over it.
value.description: F0 white; F1-F5 a grid of about 140 blue halftone portraits scales up to overfill the frame; a frosted pill opens at centre (F10-F19) and types a long, specific query at about one character a frame (F22-F78). The crowd gives the problem in one image; the query's specificity makes the viewer wait for its answer, which the cut at 2.933 delivers.

value.purpose: Problem and question: a crowd, and a query that narrows it.
value.retentionDevice: Typing in progress: an unfinished sentence keeps the eye on it.
value.content: Halftone portrait wall pushed in twice; search pill typing.

value.purpose: Answer: one person survives the query and becomes real.
value.retentionDevice: Halftone held 1 s, then resolved to a photo: a delayed reveal.
value.content: Single tile on white, name typing below, halftone to photo at 4.0-4.17.

value.purpose: Proof by depth: the record is read field by field at a legible size.
value.retentionDevice: Each cut reveals a new field typing in; the viewer keeps reading.
value.content: Hero-size section label and bio line, then label column and value column in alternating close-ups.

value.purpose: Payoff of the single result: the whole record at once, with a count of further hidden fields.
value.retentionDevice: Scale release after close-ups; a 1.47 s hold.
value.content: Pull-out to the full card on white with soft shadow.

value.purpose: Scale: the single result was one of many.
value.retentionDevice: The opening's halftone returns, so the viewer recognises the crowd from the hook.
value.content: Cut to a halftone grid of cards, two-stage pull-out to about 150 small cards, hold.

value.purpose: Claim: the method in one two-part line, made out of the crowd itself.
value.retentionDevice: Matter morph: cards become dots become a stream that writes words.
value.content: Centre-out ripple to dots, cone, stream; two short phrases left and right on one baseline.

value.purpose: Sign-off: product label and mark on the same baseline as the line.
value.retentionDevice: Empty white beat before it, so the mark arrives on silence of the picture.
value.content: Product label left, mark and wordmark right; blur in, hold, blur out to white.

payoff.value: The full record pulled back into view (8.4-11.07 s), then revealed to be one tile of a crowd of equally full records (11.07-13.66 s).

callToAction.value: Soft: a product label and the mark, small (about 3-5% of frame height) on white, with no URL, button or offer; the final three frames are empty white.

whyItWorks: One object carried through every state (crowd tile, person, record, crowd tile, dot, letter), so 19.8 s feel like a single thought rather than a list of features.

Bookended structure: two stepped push-ins from crowd to one at the start, two stepped pull-outs from one to crowd at 11-13.7 s, with the same blue halftone as the hinge. The return makes the scale claim without a number.

Interface shown at reading size: field labels at about 6% cap height and the section label at 57% of frame width, cut in close-ups, so each field is legible for about a second instead of being a mock at 1% text height.
Every cut lands on something already moving (a glyph typing, a pan, a tilt), which hides the jump and keeps attention on the content.

Restraint in palette and type: white, light grey and one cobalt; one neutral grotesque in mixed case; small type everywhere except the one hero word. The density comes from the product, not from decoration.
Breaths before each transformation (1.47 s on the full record, 0.47 s on the still grid, five white frames before the sign-off) give each new state a clean start.
